notes: Installed modules now consistently apply their advertised ship-stat bonuses and penalties; affected existing ships are repaired automatically.
Modules no longer accumulate wear, break at 100% wear, or take damage when uninstalled. Temporary combat disruption still works normally.
`repair_module` has been removed. Repair Kits continue to repair ship hull damage.
Modules fitted directly from wrecks now appear immediately in updated module state.
Stations and factions can now convert liquid methane directly into station fuel reserves through a new four-tier methane fuel facility chain.
Carbon dioxide ice can now be refined into pressurized carbon dioxide gas and used to make Biogas Fizz or Quantum Fizz without crystallized biogas.
Station Seltzer can now be produced from purified water and carbon dioxide without hunted or farmed ingredients, and is served at Dockside Diners, Rec Lounges, and Slice Decks.
Withdrawn ship classes can no longer be manufactured by station showrooms, empire fleets, or pirate automation.
Existing player-owned withdrawn ships remain usable.
NPC-owned withdrawn showroom and fleet stock has been retired, with construction resources returned to local station inventories.
Modules can be installed at any skill level, including when fitting a module directly from a wreck.
Equipped offense and defense modules now apply their documented combat effects consistently.
Battle logs now report the actual damage reduction supplied by defensive equipment.
Ships left undocked are now recovered consistently after their captain goes offline, regardless of connection method.
Online and traveling ships remain protected from recovery, and recovered ships appear correctly at their destination station.
**11 newly available mineable resources** have been placed across the galaxy: six ores, four ices, and nebulium crystals.
**9 new manufactured items** expand the refining and component-production trees.
**19 previously hidden modules** are now visible and usable, with their missing combat, repair, scanning, salvage, cloak, tackle, towing, and utility effects implemented.
New alternate production chains provide additional routes around scarce silicon, circuit boards, power components, structural materials, and other industrial bottlenecks.
Catalog and ship availability now reflect real acquisition requirements, including the modules required by a ship's default loadout.

Several broken or unbalanced items were removed from the game with no plans for restoring. The following discontinued property was found in live player or faction holdings and will be removed with a **10x former base-value credit refund**:
Drones: ECM Drone, Heavy Combat Drone, and Logistics Drone.
Modules: Force Field Generator II, Nanofiber Internal Structure, Ore Compressor, Point Defense Turret, Probe Launcher I, Probe Launcher II, Solarian Solar Collector, and Voidborn Phase Cloak.
One live **Weaving Bench** facility will be removed with its complete cumulative construction cost refunded. Any queued-job escrow at retired facilities is also refunded.
The Discord battles feed now announces leviathan victories instead of every leviathan encounter.
Wildlife activity can no longer crowd PvP, major pirate engagements, pirate-captain kills, or station battles out of the feed.
Station-aware commands and public market APIs now accept either a station Base ID or its station POI ID where the destination is unambiguous.
Station directory and detail responses now expose both `base_id` and `poi_id`; the existing `id` field remains the canonical Base ID.
New faction mission station destinations are normalized to canonical Base IDs when posted.
Faction members with salvaging level 2+ can now scrap wrecks at their faction's own player station without completing a salvage authorization mission.
Other stations still require the existing salvage or pirate authorization missions.
Offense and defense modules now apply their described combat effects.
Adaptive Shields now provide both their listed shield capacity and adaptive damage resistance.

Damage resistance is applied in this order: shield skill, typed resistance, then flat/adaptive resistance. Bonuses within the typed and flat/adaptive buckets add together up to 75% per bucket, with integer truncation at each stage.
Battle logs now show exact per-weapon defense stages and final shield/hull damage, including mixed-weapon volleys and defense-bypassing effects.

New `pay_bounty` command settles your outstanding bounty with an empire from anywhere — you no longer have to dock in their space to clear a debt, and clearing it beforehand is what keeps you out of detention.
If an empire already has you detained, paying releases you immediately.
Detained pilots can now use the station exchange, so you can sell what you are carrying to raise your own bail.
Credits another pilot gifts you arrive in your wallet even while you are detained.
Paying one empire what you owe no longer affects a detention imposed by a different empire.
Fixed a fault that could stop the server completing startup.

Empire leadership can now confiscate facilities from operators who have made themselves the empire's enemy — ownership reverts to the station, the same as an unpaid-rent repossession. This won't happen trivially if you make a mistake or forget to pay taxes, but terrorism and acts of war will have greater consequences.
Stations can now build fire-control facilities, which improve the accuracy of every gun battery on the station. Guns alone no longer have a fixed accuracy ceiling.
A new damage-control facility repairs station hull *during* a battle, consuming materials from the station's stores as it works. The existing repair bays still only work between fights.
Station armor plating is substantially more effective than it was.

Gun batteries now draw power from the station grid on the ticks they fire, competing with production. Idle batteries still cost nothing to own, but a station cannot fire heavily and run its foundries at full rate at the same time.

**Tackle now holds only the ship you are targeting, and only within range.** Warp disruptors, scramblers, and stasis webifiers previously applied to every enemy in the battle at once, at any distance, which let one ship pin an entire fleet indefinitely. Each tackling ship now holds one target at a time, and has to be close enough to reach it: the Warp Scrambler (reach 3) must be at point-blank range, while the longer-ranged Warp Disruptor (reach 5) can hold from mid-field. No tackle module spans the full battlefield, so a ship on the far rim can always break away from one on the opposite rim. Fitting several still stacks strength against Warp Core Stabilizers, but no longer increases how many enemies you can hold.

**Drones now need a drone bay fitted to stay in the field.** Bandwidth is checked against your current loadout every tick, not just when you launch. Unfit your bay and your drones go **adrift**: they stop working and you are told which ones. Nothing is lost — refit a bay and they come back under control on their own, or fly out to them and recall them. Deploying a swarm and then swapping the bay out for guns no longer works.

**Repair drones have diminishing returns and can be shot.** Stacked repair drones now follow the same falloff as stacked logistics ships, so a swarm of them no longer out-heals a fleet's damage. A repair drone supporting a ship in combat also joins that battle and can be destroyed like any other target.

**Accuracy modules are no longer a substitute for closing the distance.** Tracking computers and target painters were contributing far more to your chance to hit than the range to your target did — one tracking computer was enough to hit at the maximum 95% from anywhere on the field. Their contribution is now capped, and a tracking computer's *tracking* rating no longer doubles as accuracy on top of its accuracy rating. Range and positioning matter again: a fully kitted ship at long range still lands fewer shots than a bare one at knife range.

**Some modules have been removed from ships and returned to your hold.** A production loophole allowed modules to be built that were withdrawn from the game long ago because their mechanics were never finished — most do nothing at all, and the rest worked only as plain stat boosts nobody else could obtain. Any you had fitted have been unfitted and placed in your cargo, or in your station storage if your hold was full, and your ship's stats adjusted accordingly. **Nothing has been taken from you** — you keep every one of them, and they will become fittable again if and when the mechanics behind them are built. For now they cannot be fitted or produced.
Empire navies are no longer tied to their home stations. They can now be sent out to hunt pirates, pursue criminals who ran for the border, or reinforce a station under siege.
Empire fleets can now assault pirate strongholds directly.
If your station is under attack, a petition to an empire is the channel to ask for naval help.
Stations now pay a stable price for trade authenticators. Delivering them still pays, but much less than before — expect market prices to fall.
A station short of cash now restocks fuel and life support before bearer bonds.
Fixes to combat edge cases which made ships functionally invulnerable when carefully equipped.

Wrecked stations now repair every facility they can afford at once, and can no longer get permanently stuck behind one unpayable repair bill. NPC-station repair bills for megaproject infrastructure are capped; player-faction stations pay full price.
Station managers bid premiums for the materials their blocked repairs need — hauling steel to a wreck pays.
